extension.summary: A Streamlined Utility Tool for Kodi
extension.description: No Bloatware, no Nonsense! Just Keep your Kodi sharp and clean with this utility tool... Now with a Custom Wizard. The "++" fork backs up and restores over Kodi's VFS, so Backup Location / Restore can point straight at a network share (nfs://, smb://) or any VFS path, not just local storage.
extension.news: 2026.07.08.1 - New: the "Restore Complete" prompt now also offers to rename THIS device. A restore clones the other box's name (Settings > Services > General), so a box built from a "base" backup comes up with the source box's name. On the first boot after a restore you can rename it right there (or keep it), then set the video cache buffer as before. The new name is written so it sticks even if the box is unplugged instead of closed cleanly. Still asks only once, and never delays boot. 2026.07.07.6 - New: after a restore + restart, EZ Maintenance++ offers to set the video cache buffer to the size recommended for THIS device. A restore clones the other box's settings, so the buffer can end up sized for the wrong device (it should match this device's RAM). On the first boot after a restore you get a "Restore Complete" prompt: set the recommended size, choose your own, or keep what you have. It asks only once. 2026.07.07.5 - Honest restart prompt: on Fire TV / Android, Kodi cannot restart itself (only desktop Kodi can), so after a restore the prompt now says "Kodi needs to close to finish. Close Kodi now, then reopen it" instead of the misleading "Restart now?". On desktop it still says "Restart". 2026.07.07.4 - Fix: the "wipe clean before restore" step now shows a progress bar ("Wiping the device clean...") instead of a blank, hung-looking gap. On a device with lots of files the wipe can take a while; before, the screen sat empty for up to ~90 seconds between the download finishing and the restore window appearing. It now shows a moving bar the whole time. 2026.07.07.3 - New: Restore now asks "Wipe this device clean before restoring?" - "Yes" makes a clean clone (it removes the current add-ons and settings first, then restores); "No" merges the backup over what is already there. The wipe is SAFE: the chosen backup is staged and validated first, and the box is only wiped once the zip is confirmed good, so a missing or corrupt backup never wipes anything. - IMPORTANT crash fix: restoring a large backup could crash Kodi partway through on Fire TV sticks (the progress screen redrew a changing filename thousands of times and overran the on-screen text renderer). The restore progress no longer shows the per-file name; it shows "Extracting file X of Y" and updates less often, so it no longer crashes, while the bar still moves and always finishes. - Restore now writes your settings (userdata) before add-ons, so if an extract is ever interrupted your irreplaceable settings are already in place and only re-downloadable add-ons would be missing. 2026.07.07.2 - Restore now restores your backup EXACTLY as taken. The previous release re-stamped the backup/restore paths after a restore; that is removed. A restore is a plain extract, and you set the backup location yourself in Settings. 2026.07.07.1 - The add-on's main menu now shows the installed version as a plain line at the bottom (below Settings), e.g. "EZ Maintenance++ 2026.07.07.1". It is read live from the add-on, so it is always accurate. 2026.07.07.0 - IMPORTANT fix (real root cause of the blank Settings screen): Kodi's own Settings dialog for this add-on rendered every label blank because this add-on's settings.xml used plain-text labels and shipped no language file - Kodi resolves settings labels as numeric string ids, so plain text came back empty. This was NOT a Kodi engine bug (a prior release misdiagnosed it as one); a control add-on's Settings dialog renders fine on the same box. Every label now has a proper string id backed by a resources/language strings.po, so the native Settings dialog renders correctly - the standard, supported way. The empty "One-Tap Restore" settings tab is gone (its hidden pin storage moved into Backup/Restore); your stored settings, One-Tap pins, and Dropbox sign-in are unchanged. 2026.07.05.0 - IMPORTANT reliability fix: Kodi's own Settings dialog for this add-on could render completely blank (no categories, no controls, sometimes even the wrong add-on's name in the header) - live-confirmed as a Kodi engine bug, not something fixable in this add-on's settings.xml, reproducing even on a fresh install and on unrelated Kodi-team add-ons. Settings now opens a custom in-app screen instead, covering Backup Location, Restore Location, Destination (Local/Network/Dropbox), keep-count, Dropbox sign-in/keys, and all Maintenance options - reading and writing the exact same settings storage as before, just displayed through a screen that actually works. Backup/Restore also no longer falls back to the broken dialog when the backup location isn't set yet; it opens the same working screen. - The settings.xml schema itself was also migrated to Kodi's modern versioned format (a real, separate defect from the dialog rendering bug above) so the underlying setting values load correctly regardless of which screen displays them. 2026.07.04.6 - The in-app "What's New" display was showing the ENTIRE changelog going back to 2020 (250+ lines) in Kodi's small Add-on Information popup - trimmed to the most recent versions. The full history is unchanged and still lives in this add-on's changelog.txt and in git history; nothing was deleted, only shortened what Kodi displays in that one popup. 2026.07.04.5 - IMPORTANT reliability fix: the 2026.07.04.4 fix wasn't enough - a second real device log showed the fallback copy ALSO failing to read the same local file, proving Kodi's own VFS layer cannot read this backup's freshly-built local zip through any entry point, even though it always correctly reports that file's size. The local file is now read with plain Python file I/O instead of Kodi's VFS for both the copy and its retry, matching how this add-on already builds and validates that same file elsewhere. A remote source (nfs://, smb://) is unaffected and still goes through Kodi's VFS as before. 2026.07.04.4 - IMPORTANT reliability fix: large backup/restore copies to a network share could fail every time with "size mismatch (0 != total)". Root cause found via a real device log: this is a regression from the 2026.07.01.0 progress-bar rewrite, which replaced a plain whole-file copy with a chunked read/write loop so it could show a gauge and support cancel - on some devices (confirmed: tvOS/Apple TV) that chunked reader can come back completely empty on a freshly-built local file even though its size is reported correctly, so no amount of retrying the same chunked copy could ever succeed. The copy now falls back to the original, reliable whole-file copy (itself now also size-verified) whenever the chunked path can't ship the correct number of bytes, instead of giving up. 2026.07.04.3 - Diagnostic only (not a fix): if a backup/restore copy still reports "size mismatch" after the previous release's settle wait, the log now also records how many bytes were actually read and written on that attempt. The previous fix's theory (a large NFS write needing a moment to commit) turned out not to fully explain a real failure still seen after that fix shipped - this pinpoints which side of the copy is actually at fault so the real fix can be targeted correctly instead of guessed again. 2026.07.04.2 - IMPORTANT reliability fix: a large backup/restore copy over NFS could report "size mismatch" and fail even though the write fully succeeded - Kodi's NFS client can take a moment to commit a big write server-side, and checking the size the instant the write closes could catch it too early. The size check now waits briefly for it to settle before giving up, instead of discarding a completed copy and retrying the whole transfer from scratch. 2026.07.04.1 - Fix: backup/restore destination now strips an explicit :2049 port that Kodi's own NFS browse dialog bakes into the path - that form breaks Kodi's NFS write path (VfsCopyError / 0-byte copy). 2026.07.02.0 - Backup/Restore/One-Tap network copies now retry a failed NFS/SMB write instead of giving up on the first try. Kodi's own NFS client can leave a connection stale right after it auto-closes an idle one; a same-instant retry used to hit that same broken connection and fail again, so backups could fail even though the share was fine. Now a failed copy waits a few seconds and tries again (up to 3 attempts total) before reporting failure, giving Kodi room to open a fresh connection. 2026.07.01.1 - IMPORTANT data-loss fix: "Keep how many backups" (rotation) no longer deletes a backup you renamed. It now only prunes the tool's own automatic backups (the ones ending in a date stamp); any backup you renamed, or a "keep" in the name, is protected and never auto-deleted. Renaming a backup used to make it the FIRST one deleted; now it is the safest. Applies to Dropbox and Network/Local. - "Pick a Dropbox backup" is now a live read of the account you are actually signed into. If you switch Dropbox accounts, the list updates to the new account instead of showing the old account's files until the token refreshed. - Menu tidy: the "[ + ]" prefix on empty One-Tap Restore slots is gone.

extension.summary: Shared install library for the Tony.7.Bones Setup add-ons
extension.description: Internal Python library used by the Tony.7.Bones Setup add-ons. It is not runnable on its own and does not appear on the home screen; it provides the shared add-on install, dependency-resolution and Kodi-integration machinery the Setup add-ons depend on.
extension.news: v1.7.0: Fix: apply_iptv's staged-provider consumption assumed every m3uPath/customTvGroupsFile was a portable special:// reference needing a local copy; a live network reference (no local staging at all) hit a same-file copy that silently failed, dropping an Xtream-mode provider entirely. Now carried through unchanged when it is already a direct, absolute location. v1.6.0: Fix: EZ Maintenance++ backup now actually installs (previously wired but never called). Fix: Guided wizard re-checks real Foundation config, not just skin state. v1.5.0: Onboarding self-creates the _T7B/kodi/{backups,iptv,media,repositories,rss} device tree (ensure_device_dirs / DEVICE_STAGING_SUBDIRS); IPTV staging is injected only when the iptv/ dir actually holds artifacts. (v1.4.0: Device-resident master env at the _T7B/ brand root (dot-optional env.<device>), ordered env-source search (brand root -> staging _T7B/kodi/ -> legacy kodi/tony.7.bones/ -> profile-local), persistent master never deleted, self-scaffolding placeholder template when no env exists. (v1.3.0: Ordered env-source layer — BOX_ENV_PATH (pushed env wins) then the profile-local env, with read_first_env/box_env_paths/delete_box_envs helpers and terminal deletes covering every candidate; SETUP_API 2. (v1.2.0: Modular Setup layers — re-entrant apply_foundation/apply_iptv/apply_addons (each leaves a complete working box), installed-state probes + assert_box_complete (dependency-closure walk), the PVR-disabled config window for pvr.iptvsimple instance-settings writes, staged-IPTV artifact consumption (host-built m3u/groups/instance files), keep-skin activation hardening (verify-then-re-assert with skinshortcuts quiescence), and the SETUP_API version guard.)

extension.description: Installs repositories and add-ons for a personal Kodi build.
extension.news: v2.1.0: Lockstep bump for script.module.tony7bones 1.7.0 (the IPTV staged-provider live-network-reference fix). v2.0.0: Add a custom Setup icon (gear + checkmark) so Kodi's add-on browser no longer shows a blank placeholder. v1.9.0: Fix: EZ Maintenance++ backup now actually installs (previously wired but never called). Fix: Guided wizard re-checks real Foundation config, not just skin state. v1.8.0: Setup creates the device folder structure (_T7B/kodi/{backups,iptv,media,repositories,rss}) on every run if missing — Express, Guided, and the no-env wizard all scaffold it. (v1.7.0: Setup reads each box's own env.<device> from /storage/emulated/0/_T7B/ (created as a disabled placeholder if missing) so a box self-configures with no computer; the device-resident master env is persistent and never deleted; unattended Express + Guided wizard unchanged. (v1.6.0: Launching Setup with no device env now opens the Guided wizard — choose Foundation / IPTV / Add-ons, or "Install everything with defaults" — so a manual launch installs nothing until chosen; the unattended Express one-tap still runs whenever a device env is present. (v1.5.0: Modular Setup — Express one-tap unchanged; three standalone layers (run_foundation, run_iptv, run_addons), each leaving a complete working box; Guided wizard via SETUP_MODE=guided with per-gate restarts and the Model A lifecycle (Setup persists across gates, env consumed at Finish, then self-uninstalls); shared-library SETUP_API compatibility guard. (v1.4.0: Per-device config from one .env — the provisioner derives a per-device tony7bones.env and the Setup reads it to set weather (up to 5 locations + optional Weatherbit/OpenWeatherMap keys), IPTV (custom groups + m3u/EPG), and RSS feeds, then removes it; built-in defaults when absent. (v1.3.3: Live TV now loads only the custom channel groups — the Setup enforces pvr.iptvsimple's "Only load TV channels in groups" (tvChannelGroupsOnly) alongside the custom-groups mode + file. (v1.3.2: Reliable skin activation — Setup now ACCEPTS Kodi's "Keep this skin?" confirmation when it switches to Estuary MOD V2, so the choice persists across the end-of-setup restart instead of reverting to stock Estuary. (v1.3.1: Adds three File-Manager sources — "special://home" (special://home), "special://kodi" (/storage/emulated/0/kodi/), and ".tony.7.bones" (https://tony7bones.github.io/). New sources de-dupe by name and path; and ANY existing source pointing at the repo URL — with or without a trailing slash, under any label — is renamed to ".tony.7.bones". (v1.3.0: one-shot also installs + activates the Estuary MOD V2 skin and the MOD V2+ patch auto-applies via its service.)

extension.summary: Lean enhancements for Estuary MOD V2
extension.description: A small, non-destructive set of enhancements for skin.estuary.modv2 (Estuary MOD V2), built fresh against the Omega release. Reorders the gear Settings menu so Skin Settings sits above Media sources, and adds a dedicated "Tony.7.Bones MOD V2++" Skin Settings category that is home to our tweaks. The System Info overlay is hidden by default (toggle renamed "Disable System Info overlay"), the top-bar weather icons default to the Outline HD set (resource.images.weathericons.outline-hd), and the clock and navigation wordmark each have a per-item toggle that defaults to the stock look. The category also carries in-tab Apply and Restore buttons. Run after installing or updating skin.estuary.modv2. Apply and Restore are both available — original files are backed up once and never overwritten, and Restore reverts every change cleanly.
extension.news: v1.4.10: New V2++ icon - the bottom wordmark now reads "Tony.7.Bones V2++". v1.4.9: Renamed to Estuary MOD V2++ (the display name and the "Tony.7.Bones MOD V2++" Skin Settings category) to match the ++ line. Same add-on id, no functional change. v1.4.8: Home menu reliability fix — (re)deploying our home menu now CLEARS script.skinshortcuts' built cache for skin.estuary.modv2 AND drops the built menu hash in one step, so skinshortcuts always regenerates from OUR trimmed menu (Live TV, Movies/TV shows, Add-ons, Favorites, Weather) on the next boot. Defeats the caching race where a live skin-switch built and cached the stock Estuary menu before our menu deployed, leaving the wrong menu on a fresh box. (v1.4.7: First-boot persistence fix — the look settings (weather in the header, Outline HD icons, plain Power/Settings/Search backgrounds, classic power menu) now write straight to settings.xml on apply, so a freshly-provisioned box shows them on the FIRST boot instead of stock; the boot service also re-applies them if they are ever missing (settings-aware gate). (v1.4.6: Home menu now deploys the exact saved layout verbatim — the six-item trim, Movies/TV shows open POV, TV opens the Guide, the Favorites relabel, and the Movies List / TV Shows List widgets — and self-heals (re-deploys) if a skin update or a build race ever resets it. (v1.4.5: Home menu now reliably trims to six items even when Setup's live skin-switch raced script.skinshortcuts into caching the full stock menu — the service detects the un-trimmed menu and rebuilds it on the next boot. (v1.4.4: the auto-apply service now waits for the Home screen to actually render (not just for the skin to be set) before patching, fixing the occasional blank/unfinished home after a restart. (v1.4.3: new V2+ icon; channel numbers off. v1.4.2: TV opens the Guide, Favourites→Favorites, six home widgets hidden.)
